key_insight: Specialized, physics-informed ML force fields are needed to reliably simulate far-from-equilibrium materials dynamics because general-purpose MLIPs break down on reactive, strained, and nonlocal phenomena.
engineering_relevance: For fracture and damage modeling, these tailored potentials can extend atomistic simulation to larger length and time scales, but only if they are validated against the specific observables relevant to the target failure process.
method: Assess MLIP design trade-offs for dynamics: strained-state coverage, message-passing cost, and nonlocal interactions.
Use task-specific specialization for challenging regimes such as electrified interfaces, open systems, multiphase evolution, and large-scale fracture.
Benchmark models with observable-specific validation rather than relying on zero-shot near-equilibrium accuracy.
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes four demanding application contexts and uses them to compare how well specialized MLIPs capture intended dynamical observables versus broad pretrained models.
watch_item: Specialization can improve performance, but undersampled high-strain states and high-order architectures may still limit robustness and computational scalability.
paper_title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
